a1.say: Let's solve Paint Bucket Fill, using the DFS approach.

a1.cap: image[r][c] is a pixel color. Starting from pixel (sr, sc), repaint it and every pixel of the same original color connected to it (up, down, left, right) with color. Return the image.
a1.say: image at r, c is a pixel color. Starting from pixel (sr, sc), repaint it and every pixel of the same original color connected to it (up, down, left, right) with color. Return the image.

lines: image[r][c] is a pixel color. Starting from pixel (sr, sc), repaint it and every pixel of the same original color connected to it (up, down, left, right) with color. Return the image.

a1.say: For example, with image equals 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 0, 1, 0, 1, sr equals 1, sc equals 1, color equals 2, the answer is 2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 0, 2, 0, 1.

a1.cap: Remember the starting color. Recursively repaint a pixel if it still has that color, then spread to its four neighbours. If the new color equals the old one, there's nothing to do.
